# Categorise Customer Feedback from Online Forms with Cohere

Managing customer feedback can feel like sifting through a mountain of comments, but it's crucial for understanding your customers. This guide will show you how to use Cohere, an AI platform, to automatically sort new feedback into categories. By the end, you'll be able to quickly spot trends and make informed decisions for your business.

## Before you start
- An active Cohere account (a free tier is usually available for experimentation).
- Access to the Cohere web Playground (a web interface to test AI models without coding).
- A few examples of customer feedback you want to categorise.
- Roughly 10-15 minutes to follow along.

## Step 1 — Log in to your Cohere account
Start by heading to the Cohere website and logging into your account. This is your gateway to their powerful AI models.
Once you're on the Cohere homepage, look for a "Log in" button, usually found in the top-right corner. Click it and enter your email address and password. If you don't have an account, there'll be a "Sign up" or "Get Started" option that will guide you through creating one.
You'll know it worked when you see your Cohere dashboard or main account page.

## Step 2 — Navigate to the Playground
The Cohere Playground is where you can experiment with their AI models directly through a web interface, without needing to write any code.
On your Cohere dashboard, look for a navigation menu, usually on the left-hand side or at the top of the screen. Find and click on the option labelled "Playground". This will open a new interface designed for interacting with their different AI models, like a sandbox where you can play and see what the AI can do.
If it looks different, search for terms like "Workbench", "Experiment", or "Models" within the navigation.
You'll know it worked when you see a large text input area and options to select different AI models on the screen.

## Step 3 — Select the 'Generate' model
Cohere offers several AI models, each designed for different tasks. For classifying feedback, we'll use the "Generate" model to create a custom prompt that tells the AI how to sort your text.
Within the Playground, you'll see a section to choose your AI model. Look for a dropdown menu or a list of options, and select "Generate". Below this, you might also see options for model versions, but for now, just pick the default or most recent 'Generate' model available. This model is like a versatile writer that can follow instructions to produce specific types of text, including classifications.
You'll know it worked when the Playground interface updates to show options specific to text generation, like temperature or length controls.

## Step 4 — Input your feedback and categories as a prompt
Now you'll tell the AI what to do by giving it a clear instruction, which we call a 'prompt'. The prompt will include your customer feedback and a list of possible categories.
In the main text input area of the Playground, type your instruction. Start by clearly stating what the feedback is and then list the categories you want the AI to choose from. Make sure your categories are specific and distinct.
💬 Example: `Customer Feedback: "The website kept crashing when I tried to pay, and the shipping was much slower than advertised." Categorise this into one of the following: Website Issue, Shipping Issue, Product Quality, Customer Service, Billing Problem.`
You'll know it worked when you've typed your feedback and categories into the prompt box, ready for the AI to process.

## Step 5 — Run the model and review the output
Once your prompt is ready, it's time to send it to the Cohere AI model and see its classification.
Look for a "Run", "Generate", or "Submit" button, typically located at the bottom of the prompt input area or on the right-hand side of the screen. Click this button to send your instruction to the AI. The AI will then process your feedback based on the categories you provided. A new section will appear, displaying the AI's response, which should be the category it identified for your feedback.
You'll know it worked when Cohere shows you the AI's generated response, which should be one of the categories you listed.

## Step 6 — Refine your categories for better accuracy
If the AI's classification isn't quite right, you can easily adjust your categories or the prompt to get more accurate results. This is a common part of working with AI.
Think about why the AI might have picked the wrong category. Were your categories too broad? Did they overlap? Or was the feedback too vague? Go back to the prompt in the Playground and try rephrasing your categories to be more distinct or adding more specific examples if possible. Then, click "Run" again. This iterative process helps the AI learn exactly how you want your feedback sorted.
💬 Example: `Customer Feedback: "My package arrived two days late, and the tracking information was never updated." Categorise this into one of the following: Delivery Delay, Tracking Glitch, Product Damage, Returns Process.`
You'll know it worked when the AI consistently categorises your feedback into the specific types you intended, making your analysis much clearer.

## Common mistakes
-   **Too vague categories:** Using categories like "Other" or "General Issue" can lead to unhelpful sorting. Instead, try to break down broad categories into more specific ones, even if you have many. The more distinct your categories, the clearer the AI's output.
-   **Not providing enough context:** If the feedback is short or ambiguous, the AI might struggle to classify it correctly. When possible, include slightly more detail in your prompt about what you're asking it to do.
-   **Expecting perfection on the first try:** AI models learn from your input, so it's normal to need a few rounds of refinement. Don't get discouraged if the first few attempts aren't perfect; adjust your prompt and categories, and you'll see improvement. This approach can help classify, but it cannot understand the deep emotional context or nuances that only a human can fully grasp.

## What this means for you
-   **For your business or work:** Automatically categorising customer feedback lets you quickly identify recurring issues, track customer sentiment over time, and prioritise improvements. Imagine instantly knowing if there's a surge in "Shipping Delays" or "Website Login Issues" after a new update.
-   **If you're just getting started:** Begin with a small set of feedback examples and a clear, simple list of 3-5 categories. Experiment in the Cohere Playground to get a feel for how the AI responds before thinking about integrating it into your workflow.

## Try it now
Open the Cohere Playground, select the "Generate" model, and paste a piece of customer feedback you've received. Then, add a line like "Categorise this into: Price Issue, Product Quality, Delivery Problem, Customer Service." and click "Run" to see how it sorts.
